properties.name: The 0.79.0 install near-miss came from a recipe the maintainer's agent wrote in chat, not from anything reflow2 ships. Its `ln -sf … reflow2` would have replaced the installer's wrapper. Its rollback copy hard-coded 0.76.0 and came after the install. Its `loop_status | head -40` check and its backup order were its own
properties.statement:
From art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05: entries [defect] (lines 358-367) and [friction] (lines 362-365) of 2026-10-05, and the recipe steps quoted in the [friction] entries at lines 338-349. Recorded so that a later reader does not look for these steps in reflow2.

WHAT HAPPENED. On 2026-10-05 the maintainer's own agent (the main dev_reflow2 hub session) wrote a manual 0.79.0 upgrade recipe in chat for the work laptop. reflow2 shipped none of it. Searched on main 7f5984ec5: no document or script contains `ln -s`, no upgrade check reads `head -40`, and getting-started/UPDATING.md has no backup step. The v0.79.0 release notes say only "See CHANGELOG.md for what changed", plus the container image.

THE RECIPE'S ERRORS, each the cause of a near-miss:
1. `ln -sf ~/.local/bin/reflow2-mcp ~/.local/bin/reflow2` assumed a machine with only the binary. On a machine set up by reflow2_install.py, `~/.local/bin/reflow2` is a shell wrapper that handles init, update, install, check and hook. The reporter checked first and did not run it. Measured on a scratch copy of what it would have left: `reflow2 init`, `update`, `install` and `check` each fail with the binary's "error: unrecognized subcommand", and the installer cannot then repair it (fact:defect-the-installer-cannot-repair-a-reflow2-command-that-is-a-symlink-to-the-binary-2026-10-05).
2. The rollback copy `cp … reflow2-mcp.0.76.0` hard-coded the old version, and came after the install, so it would have saved 0.79.0 under a 0.76.0 name.
3. The order (export, back up, then upgrade) was given after the binary had been replaced: installed 11:55, recipe run 11:59.
4. Its "anything unexported?" check, `--call loop_status | head -40`, reads the first 40 lines of a reply whose keys are alphabetical, so the artifact block comes first.

WHAT IN REFLOW2 LET IT BE WRONG is recorded separately, as reflow2's own gaps: fact:root-cause-reflow2-documents-no-binary-only-install-and-no-way-to-tell-a-wrapper-machine-2026-10-05, fact:root-cause-the-update-path-has-no-step-before-the-binary-is-replaced-2026-10-05 and fact:recurrence-a-store-ahead-of-its-export-is-not-said-where-an-upgrade-check-reads-on-0-79-0-2026-10-05.

FOR THE MAINTAINER'S SESSIONS: nothing checks a recipe written in chat for a user's machine. Build it from UPDATING.md and the machine's own state (`head -2 ~/.local/bin/reflow2`, `reflow2-mcp --version`). Anything it needs that the document lacks is a gap in the document.
